We were thinking of a breakout room, so I may just give it a quick shout out on ACD 👍 Hi guys, I just tried sending EIP1559 txs over TurboGeth/Besu/Nethermind but all of them failed. If I just try to serialize a tx such that it represents the bytes which we use for the transactions trie (so for EIP1559 these bytes start with `0x02`) then nodes do not accept it. However, if I re-RLP the byte sequence (so the one starting with `0x02`) then I get a valid RLP which can be directly decoded and nodes seem to accept this. This, however, breaks some stuff like in web3; ```javascript var Tx = require('ethereumjs-tx').Transaction; var privateKey = Buffer.from('e331b6d69882b4cb4ea581d88e0b604039a3de5967688d3dcffdd2270c0fd109', 'hex'); var rawTx = { nonce: '0x00', gasPrice: '0x09184e72a000', gasLimit: '0x2710', to: '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000', value: '0x00', data: '0x7f7465737432000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000600057' } var tx = new Tx(rawTx, {'chain':'ropsten'}); tx.sign(privateKey); var serializedTx = tx.serialize(); // console.log(serializedTx.toString('hex')); // 0xf889808609184e72a00082271094000000000000000000000000000000000000000080a47f74657374320000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000006000571ca08a8bbf888cfa37bbf0bb965423625641fc956967b81d12e23709cead01446075a01ce999b56a8a88504be365442ea61239198e23d1fce7d00fcfc5cd3b44b7215f web3.eth.sendSignedTransaction('0x' + serializedTx.toString('hex')) .on('receipt', console.log); ``` If I try to `sendSignedTransaction` for a EIP1559Transaction, then I need to `rlp.encode(serializedTx)` and then send that byte sequence. This is not the case for LegacyTxs. If we want to do this (not really have any opinion yet) then this should be documented. I also find it somewhat weird that we don't "doubly" RLP these txs for the transactions trie, but we do "doubly RLP" then if we want to send them over RPC, I find this inconsistent. Is there a minimum tip for the miners to get my tx mined? I'm sure you'll have everyone rallied against me by morning. 😄 <@!508125616940515329> Yes. I'll look into it So, to be clear, do we _want_ to allow single transactions which can fill a block up to its full elasticity limit? I'm not sure the spec actually makes that clear? There's not a rule I can see in the spec which disallows it my interpretation of the spec is that a single tx should be able to use the entire elasticity limit But it would be great if this is clarified CC <@!273808422753796097> <@!574864862338088960> My personal preference is to set the max tx gas limit to the target, but I think it's more important to go with what the spec seems to say today To avoid risking delaying EIP 1559 by "changing things" So should we just make that explicit in the spec? I'm not sure where, though 😅 Maybe just a line about it in security considerations or something? I think limiting transactions to less than block gas limit just adds unnecessary complexity. Unless there is a compelling reason to add it, I generally prefer lower complexity solutions (less conditions that need to be checked). T8n doesn't do blocks. If you tell me what you'd need, (input/output), I can either add it or make a new blockt8n tool It's trivially simple to make a testcase and show that a "very large tx" makes it into a block, more problematic to demostrate, in a testcase, that such a block ia rejected. excerpts.content: I'm not sure the spec actually makes that clear?

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: There's not a rule I can see in the spec which disallows it

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: my interpretation of the spec is that a single tx should be able to use the entire elasticity limit
